transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came because everybody keeps acting like I’m the problem, like I’m making things up, but I’m not. My family and my friends keep waving bank papers around saying, “See, nothing was taken,” but those papers don’t prove anything. They can hide things in bills, and they talk about fundraisers and trips like that explains where the money went.

This has been going on for over a year, and I keep telling them I know they’re hiding my money. They won’t just tell the truth. And then they say I’m causing trouble because I keep asking, but what am I supposed to do, just let them get away with it? My cousin did that thing once with the trip plans, and everyone acted like it was normal, like I don’t understand papers or numbers, but I know when something is wrong. So… that’s why I’m here, I guess. They want someone to tell me to stop confronting them.
Do you think your family and friends are working together against you?

Yes, I mean… not like they all sit in a room with a chart or something, but they’re all saying the same thing, aren’t they? My family, my friends, everybody keeps pointing at those bank papers like that proves nothing was taken. But papers can be made to look right. Bills, fundraisers, trips—there’s always some explanation ready.

And it’s been over a year of this. I keep asking because I know my money is being hidden, and then they act like I’m the one causing problems. My cousin did that thing with the trip plans too, and everyone just brushed it off, like I’m too stupid to understand. So yes, I think they’re covering for each other until someone finally tells the truth.
Do you think someone is actively trying to harm you?

Harm me… I don’t know if I’d put it like that, like someone coming after me physically. But they are hurting me by hiding my money and then acting like I’m crazy for seeing it. My family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but those papers don’t show everything.

It’s been over a year, and every time I ask, there’s some story about bills or fundraisers or trip plans. Like my cousin with those trip plans—everyone just acted like that was normal. So yes, in that way, they’re doing something to me, and I have to keep confronting them until someone finally tells the truth.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't think your family and friends were hiding your money?

Not really. I mean, maybe before all this started, before I noticed the papers and the way everyone kept explaining things away. But for over a year now I’ve known something isn’t right. They keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but papers don’t show what people hide behind bills and fundraisers and those trip plans.

And it’s funny, because my cousin—well, not funny, but you know what I mean—when those trip plans came up, everyone acted like I was supposed to just accept it. Like because it’s written down somewhere, that makes it true. So no, not lately. I keep confronting them because if I stop, then they just get to keep pretending, and nobody tells the truth.
Do you ever have any doubts about your belief that your family and friends are hiding your money?

Doubts? Not really, no. I mean, people keep saying I should have doubts because the bank papers “prove” nothing was taken, but that’s exactly the thing—papers can be made to look right. They keep pointing at bills and fundraisers and then the trip plans, like if they say it fast enough I’ll stop asking.

And it’s been over a year, so it’s not like I just woke up one day and said this. I came in because they all keep acting like I’m making trouble, but I know they’re hiding my money. I keep having to confront them, even when it turns into a whole argument, because otherwise they just keep covering it up and nobody tells the truth.
Do you think there is one person in particular who is in charge of hiding your money and organizing the others to cover it up?

I don’t know if it’s one person, exactly. Sometimes it feels like one of them starts it and the others just go along, but then when I ask, everybody has the same kind of answer—bank papers, bills, fundraisers, trip plans, all that.

Like, they keep saying the papers prove nothing was taken, but I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money. And it’s not just one little thing, because then my cousin brings up those trip plans, and someone else says it was for bills, and then there’s some fundraiser story, and it all gets mixed together like they rehearsed it. So maybe somebody is organizing it, but I can’t say for sure who. That’s why I keep confronting them, because sooner or later one of them has to tell the truth.
Do you think the explanations your family and friends give, such as the bank papers and trip plans, are reasonable or could there be another explanation that you haven't considered?

I mean… reasonable to them, maybe, because they all say it the same way. “Look at the bank papers,” “it went to bills,” “there was a fundraiser,” “the trip plans explain it.” But that’s exactly why I came in, because they keep acting like those papers prove nothing was taken, and I’m supposed to just sit there and accept it.

I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money. And the trip thing, that bothered me, because my cousin brought it up like that was the end of the conversation, but it wasn’t. People can write things down and make it look clean. My aunt used to do that with grocery lists, she’d write things twice and then say she didn’t—sorry, that’s not the point, but it’s like that.

So no, I don’t think there’s some other explanation I haven’t considered. I think they’re using bills and fundraisers and trip plans to cover it up, and I keep confronting them because somebody has to finally tell the truth.
Have you ever had a time, even for a brief moment, where you didn't believe your family and friends were hiding your money?

No… I mean, maybe people think I should have a moment like that, but I don’t. It’s been over a year, and I know they’re hiding my money.

They keep saying, “Look at the bank papers,” like that proves nothing was taken, but papers don’t settle it for me. Then somebody brings up bills, or a fundraiser, or those trip plans, and it all turns into this big mess. My cousin talks fast when she explains things too, like when we were kids and she’d try to get out of chores—sorry, I know that’s not what you asked.

But no, I haven’t really stopped believing it. That’s why I came in, because they keep acting like I’m the problem, and I have to keep confronting them until somebody finally tells the truth.
Do you think it's possible that you could be mistaken about your family and friends hiding your money?

Mistaken? No… I don’t think so. That’s why I came in, because they keep telling me the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money.

And then it’s always something else—bills, fundraisers, those trip plans. My cousin brings up the trip plans like that explains everything, and it reminds me of how people used to pass notes in school and pretend they didn’t—well, anyway. It just feels covered up. So I don’t think I’m mistaken. I have to keep confronting them until somebody tells the truth.
Do you think it's possible for you to change your mind about your family and friends hiding your money?

I don’t see how I could change my mind unless they actually tell the truth. They keep saying those bank papers prove nothing was taken, and it’s like everyone wants me to just nod along, but I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money.

And then they bring in all these other things—bills, fundraisers, trip plans—like piling papers on a table makes it clean. My cousin does that thing where she points at one thing and then another, and it reminds me of when people would switch stories in school when the teacher came around… anyway.

So, no, not really. I came in because I’m tired of them acting like I’m supposed to believe the cover-up. I have to keep confronting them until somebody finally says what happened.
Do you think there could be any evidence that would make you change your mind about your family and friends hiding your money?

Evidence? I mean… they keep saying the bank papers are the evidence, but those papers don’t prove anything to me. Not when for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money.

If they showed me something real—well, no, see, they always make it about bills, or the fundraiser money, or those trip plans, like if they talk fast enough I’ll get confused. My friend did that once when we were looking at receipts from a lunch thing, and everyone acted like I was making a big deal out of nothing… sorry.

I don’t think there’s evidence that would change my mind unless they finally tell the truth and say where the money is. That’s why I keep confronting them.
Do you think you will ever be able to stop thinking that your family and friends are hiding your money?

I don’t think I can just stop thinking it, no. Not when I’ve known for over a year that they’re hiding my money. They keep waving those bank papers around like that proves nothing was taken, but it doesn’t feel like proof to me.

And then they bring up bills, or that fundraiser, or the trip plans—always some other thing to cover it over. My cousin did that with the trip stuff, and it reminded me of when people would shuffle papers in school so the teacher wouldn’t see what they were really passing around… anyway.

So no, I don’t think I can stop until they tell the truth. That’s why I came in. I have to keep confronting them, because if I stop, they’ll just keep hiding it.
Do you think there's anything that could happen or anything someone could say that would make you completely change your mind about your family and friends hiding your money?

Completely change my mind? I don’t… no, I don’t think there’s anything they could say unless it was the truth. They keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but papers can be made to look clean. I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money.

And it’s always the same—bills, that fundraiser, trip plans—like they throw all these other things in front of me so I’ll stop looking at the money. My family does that, my friends too. It’s like when someone changes the subject real fast and then acts like you’re the confused one.

So no, I came in because I’m tired of it. I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell me where it is.
Do you think your belief that your family and friends are hiding your money could ever change, no matter what happens or what anyone says?

No, I don’t think it would change, not just because somebody says something. That’s the problem—they keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but I don’t believe those papers tell the whole thing.

I came in because for over a year I’ve known my family and friends are hiding my money. They keep bringing up bills, or the fundraiser, or the trip plans, like if they pile enough stuff on top of it I’ll stop asking. My aunt used to do that with mail on the kitchen table, just stack things until nobody could find what they needed—sorry, that’s not the point.

The point is, no, I don’t think it changes until they tell the truth. I have to keep confronting them until they admit where the money is.
Do you think it's possible that new information could make you question your belief that your family and friends are hiding your money?

New information? I mean… if it was real information, not those bank papers they keep showing me. They keep saying that proves nothing was taken, but I don’t trust it. I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money.

They do this thing where they bring up bills, and then that fundraiser, and then trip plans, like all these little piles of excuses. My friend once did that with receipts in a grocery bag, just kept pulling them out like it meant something, and I remember thinking, nobody keeps that many receipts unless they’re trying to bury something… sorry.

So I don’t think “new information” would make me question it unless it was them finally telling the truth. That’s why I came in. I have to keep confronting them until they say where it is.
Do you think the people hiding your money are doing it for a normal reason, like they need it, or for some other reason that might seem unusual to others?

I don’t know if they need it. They don’t talk straight enough for me to know that. They keep acting like it’s normal, like, “Look, the bank papers show nothing,” but those papers don’t prove it to me. For over a year I’ve known my family and my friends are hiding my money.

And the way they do it, with the bills and that fundraiser and then talking about trip plans—like my cousin used to do when she’d lay out school papers all over the table and then say she couldn’t find anything, but really she just didn’t want to clean it up—anyway, that’s how it feels. Like they’re covering it up with all these other things.

So maybe other people would say it sounds unusual, but to me it’s just them not telling the truth. That’s why I came in. I have to keep confronting them until they finally say where the money is.
Do you think any evidence, no matter how convincing, could ever make you believe that your family and friends are not hiding your money?

No. I mean, they keep saying “evidence,” but then it’s just those bank papers again, and they act like that should end it. But it doesn’t. I’ve known for over a year my family and my friends are hiding my money.

They bring up bills, and the fundraiser, and then trip plans, like if there’s enough noise around it I’ll get tired and stop asking. My mom used to put coupons in this little drawer and then nobody could find the scissors, and she’d say it was organized, but it wasn’t—sorry, I know that’s not what you asked.

I don’t think any paper is going to make me believe they’re not hiding it. The only thing that would matter is them telling the truth. That’s why I came in. I have to keep confronting them until they say where the money is.
Is there anything, no matter how small, that could make you slightly doubt your belief that your family and friends are hiding your money?

Slightly doubt? I don’t… no, I don’t think so. Because every time they say there’s proof, it’s the bank papers, and they keep waving those around like that fixes it. But I came in because I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money.

They’ll talk about bills, then the fundraiser, then trip plans, and it’s like when people stack boxes in front of a closet so you stop asking what’s inside—my aunt did that once with holiday decorations and nobody could get to anything for months. Anyway, that’s what it feels like. Covering it up.

So, no, not really. The only thing that would make any difference is if they finally told the truth. That’s why I have to keep confronting them until they say where it is.
Do you think there is any circumstance under which you would completely believe that your family and friends are not hiding your money?

Completely believe it? No, I don’t see how I could. They keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but that’s what they want me to look at, not the money itself. I came in because I’ve known for over a year my family and friends are hiding it.

And it’s not just one thing, it’s the bills, then that fundraiser, then suddenly talking about trip plans, like when people put a blanket over a messy couch before company comes and act like the room is clean. My friend used to do that with laundry, just shove it under the bed and say everything was fine—anyway.

No, there’s not a circumstance. Not unless they tell the truth and say where the money is. That’s why I have to keep confronting them.

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether anything could make the patient completely change her fixed belief that family and friends are hiding her money, which directly concerns delusions and resistance to contradictory evidence.

patient.answer:
Completely change my mind? I don’t… no, I don’t think there’s anything they could say unless it was the truth. They keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but papers can be made to look clean. I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money.

And it’s always the same—bills, that fundraiser, trip plans—like they throw all these other things in front of me so I’ll stop looking at the money. My family does that, my friends too. It’s like when someone changes the subject real fast and then acts like you’re the confused one.

So no, I came in because I’m tired of it. I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell me where it is.

doctor.intent: Determine the level of fixed belief about the perceived conspiracy
doctor.question: Do you think your belief that your family and friends are hiding your money could ever change, no matter what happens or what anyone says?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The question is directly asking whether the belief can change despite what happens or what anyone says, which concerns the fixed nature of the delusion.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think it would change, not just because somebody says something. That’s the problem—they keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but I don’t believe those papers tell the whole thing.

I came in because for over a year I’ve known my family and friends are hiding my money. They keep bringing up bills, or the fundraiser, or the trip plans, like if they pile enough stuff on top of it I’ll stop asking. My aunt used to do that with mail on the kitchen table, just stack things until nobody could find what they needed—sorry, that’s not the point.

The point is, no, I don’t think it changes until they tell the truth. I have to keep confronting them until they admit where the money is.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's belief is fixed or flexible
doctor.question: Do you think it's possible that new information could make you question your belief that your family and friends are hiding your money?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether new information could make the patient question or change the fixed belief about family and friends hiding money, which directly assesses delusions.

patient.answer:
New information? I mean… if it was real information, not those bank papers they keep showing me. They keep saying that proves nothing was taken, but I don’t trust it. I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money.

They do this thing where they bring up bills, and then that fundraiser, and then trip plans, like all these little piles of excuses. My friend once did that with receipts in a grocery bag, just kept pulling them out like it meant something, and I remember thinking, nobody keeps that many receipts unless they’re trying to bury something… sorry.

So I don’t think “new information” would make me question it unless it was them finally telling the truth. That’s why I came in. I have to keep confronting them until they say where it is.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of bizarre content in delusions
doctor.question: Do you think the people hiding your money are doing it for a normal reason, like they need it, or for some other reason that might seem unusual to others?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the nature and explanation of the fixed belief that family and friends are hiding the money, which directly relates to the delusion.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if they need it. They don’t talk straight enough for me to know that. They keep acting like it’s normal, like, “Look, the bank papers show nothing,” but those papers don’t prove it to me. For over a year I’ve known my family and my friends are hiding my money.

And the way they do it, with the bills and that fundraiser and then talking about trip plans—like my cousin used to do when she’d lay out school papers all over the table and then say she couldn’t find anything, but really she just didn’t want to clean it up—anyway, that’s how it feels. Like they’re covering it up with all these other things.

So maybe other people would say it sounds unusual, but to me it’s just them not telling the truth. That’s why I came in. I have to keep confronting them until they finally say where the money is.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of a fixed belief despite contradictory evidence
doctor.question: Do you think any evidence, no matter how convincing, could ever make you believe that your family and friends are not hiding your money?

target_item.name: Delusions

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether even very convincing evidence could change the patient's belief, which directly concerns the fixed, unchangeable nature of the delusion.

patient.answer:
No. I mean, they keep saying “evidence,” but then it’s just those bank papers again, and they act like that should end it. But it doesn’t. I’ve known for over a year my family and my friends are hiding my money.

They bring up bills, and the fundraiser, and then trip plans, like if there’s enough noise around it I’ll get tired and stop asking. My mom used to put coupons in this little drawer and then nobody could find the scissors, and she’d say it was organized, but it wasn’t—sorry, I know that’s not what you asked.

I don’t think any paper is going to make me believe they’re not hiding it. The only thing that would matter is them telling the truth. That’s why I came in. I have to keep confronting them until they say where the money is.

Slightly doubt? I don’t… no, I don’t think so. Because every time they say there’s proof, it’s the bank papers, and they keep waving those around like that fixes it. But I came in because I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money.

doctor.question: Do you think there is any circumstance under which you would completely believe that your family and friends are not hiding your money?

target_item.name: Delusions

target_item.reason: The question is directly asking whether the belief could change under any circumstance, which relates to the fixed, resistant nature of the delusion.

patient.answer:
Completely believe it? No, I don’t see how I could. They keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but that’s what they want me to look at, not the money itself. I came in because I’ve known for over a year my family and friends are hiding it.

And it’s not just one thing, it’s the bills, then that fundraiser, then suddenly talking about trip plans, like when people put a blanket over a messy couch before company comes and act like the room is clean. No, there’s not a circumstance. Not unless they tell the truth and say where the money is. That’s why I have to keep confronting them.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent delusional thoughts that their family and friends are hiding their money, despite evidence to the contrary, such as bank papers. This belief has been held for over a year and is not altered by reasoning or evidence. The patient's thoughts are preoccupied with this belief, and they show no significant periods of doubt, indicating a delusional disorder.
